newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 24.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
*Bank of Italy cut its key discount rate to 7.5 percent from 8.25. The Bank made it clear its move was linked to signs that inflation is heading down (all).
*Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says in an interview that the Bank's decision is a "victory". The Bank "may have wanted also to help the lira re-entry into the Erm" (Repubblica).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi won a vote of confidence in Parliament over on a government decree which seeks to inject 2 trillion lire of state funds into ailing Banco di Napoli (all).

* An agreement seems near among coalition parties as Refoundation party is expected to accept tax modifications included in the 1997 budget. But Finance minister Vincenzo Visco will have to re-write the reform to make it clear it won't hit lower incomes (all).

* Ernesto Pascale, managing director of telecom holding Stet, said remarks by head of antitrust authority Giuliano Amato were "disconcerting". Amato said that if Telecom Italia went ahead with its new "supercordless" Fido it would take advantage of its dominant position in the fixed-line phone market (all).
* The treasury said it would increase the amount of shares of energy giant Eni being offered to the Italian public in the face of heavy demand (all).

* Mark Pignatelli, a representative of London-based Barings fund management, said to the parliamentary industrial commission that foreign shareholders do not want a new capital increase in Olivetti and do not support plans to sell off some of its stake in mobile group Omnitel (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
